a young patient with an orbital malignancy and a family history of early onset cancer should undergo genetic analysis to determine the presence of LFS, and that molecular analysis is useful in determining the genetic disorder and in obtaining prognostic data.
primary orbital liposatoma in a patient with Li-Fraumani cancer family syndrome is a very rare disease, and that molecular analysis is useful for the diagnosis and treatment of this disease.

a young patient with orbital malignancy and a family history of malignancy should be evaluated for the presence of a genetic disorder, and if present, the specific genetic mutation should be determined to provide prognostic and therapeutic data for adequate treatment.

the diagnosis of an orbital tumor in a young patient, especially if associated with a family history suggestive of LFS, should lead to the performance of a molecular analysis of the tumor, which will help the clinician to better understand the prognosis of the disease.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the diagnosis of a malignancy in a patient with a family pedigree consistent with LFS should lead to a genetic analysis of the tumor and the family pedigree to confirm the diagnosis and to determine the molecular profile.
the presence of orbital liposarcomas in young patients with a family history for cancer should raise the suspicion of an underlying LFS, with the consequent need for genetic counseling.
the diagnosis of an orbital tumor in a young patient should suggest the presence not only of an underlying genetic disease, but also of an underlying genetic mutation.
